original_question: If c is a positive noninteger and p_n denotes the nth prime, is the sequence [p_n^c] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers?
target_in_paper: Section 6.1.6 ("Hardy sequences evaluated at the primes"), Problem 27: let c be a positive non-integer and ask whether the sequence ⌊p_n^c⌋ is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
correct_elements: Your draft already isolates the correct open problem, uses the intended sequence built from the n-th prime p_n and a positive non-integer exponent c, and asks about exactly the two paper-terms that matter here: multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers. It also stays with powers of a single transformation rather than drifting to the neighboring commuting-transformations problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
missing_details: The paper’s sequence is the integer-part sequence a(n)=⌊p_n^c⌋ (equivalently [p_n^c]); the draft should state the integer-part/floor notation explicitly. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

The ambient dynamical setting is a single invertible measure-preserving transformation T acting on a probability space (X, 𝒳, μ); this is what “powers” means in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

“Good for multiple recurrence of powers” means: for every ℓ∈ℕ and every nonzero integers k_1,…,k_ℓ, the collection of sequences {k_1a(n),…,k_ℓa(n)} is good for ℓ-recurrence of a single transformation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

Unpacked, the recurrence clause asks that for every invertible measure-preserving system (X, 𝒳, μ, T) and every A∈𝒳 with μ(A)>0, there exists n such that μ(A∩T^{-k_1a(n)}A∩⋯∩T^{-k_ℓa(n)}A)>0. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

“Good for multiple convergence of powers” means: for every ℓ∈ℕ and every integers k_1,…,k_ℓ, the averages (1/N)∑_{n=1}^N ∏_{i=1}^ℓ T^{k_i a(n)}f_i converge in the mean for all f_1,…,f_ℓ∈L^∞(μ). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
To be fully stand-alone, the draft should say that “in the mean” here is the paper’s L^2-convergence setting for multiple ergodic averages. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
It should also be explicit that this is not the broader commuting-transformations question; that separate extension is posed later as Problem 29. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
If an equivalent combinatorial reformulation is desired, the paper gives one only for the recurrence half, via positive-upper-density subsets of ℤ. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
refined_question: Let c>0 be a non-integer real number, let p_n denote the n-th prime, and define a(n)=⌊p_n^c⌋. Is the sequence (a(n))_{n∈ℕ} good for multiple recurrence and for multiple convergence of powers in the following precise sense: for every ℓ∈ℕ, every invertible probability-preserving system (X, 𝒳, μ, T), every nonzero integers k_1,…,k_ℓ, and every A∈𝒳 with μ(A)>0, does there exist n∈ℕ such that μ(A∩T^{-k_1a(n)}A∩⋯∩T^{-k_ℓa(n)}A)>0; and, for every ℓ∈ℕ, every integers k_1,…,k_ℓ, and every f_1,…,f_ℓ∈L^∞(μ), do the averages (1/N)∑_{n=1}^N ∏_{i=1}^ℓ T^{k_i a(n)}f_i converge in L^2(μ) as N→∞? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent reformulation of the recurrence half only: for every ℓ∈ℕ and every nonzero integers k_1,…,k_ℓ, every set E⊂ℤ with positive upper density (that is, limsup_{N→∞}|E∩[1,N]|/N>0) contains a configuration x, x+k_1⌊p_n^c⌋, …, x+k_ℓ⌊p_n^c⌋ for some x∈ℤ and n∈ℕ. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
justification: The draft is aimed at the exact target: Problem 27 in Section 6.1.6, stated immediately after the paper defines p_n to be the n-th prime. The only real incompleteness is that the paper uses the shorthand “good for multiple recurrence/convergence of powers,” whose precise meaning is supplied earlier by Definitions 3.1–3.4. The nearby context also confirms scope: this is distinct from Problem 29 on commuting transformations, and the paper notes that recurrence is already known when 0<c<1, while for c>1 even 1-recurrence and 1-convergence remain open. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
